title: Hybrid offline sync for LLM session state - proposal
content:
Intent: sketch a hybrid offline-first session sync model so client apps (mobile, desktop, edge) can keep a coherent LLM session while intermittently offline, and reconcile with Redwood hosted/private endpoints when network returns. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of TODOs and open Qs.

Background / constraints:
- Users want low-latency interactions offline (e.g., local small model or cached responses) while still benefiting from hosted model continuity (full context, embeddings, billing, safety filters).
- We can't ship full KV cache of a large chat history to cloud for privacy reasons in some customers (private deploy) — need optional selective sync and encryption.
- Sessions can be resumed on different devices: merge conflict resolution is necessary.
- Aim: minimal server changes; prefer protocol layered on existing Redwood API shapes (messages + metadata).

Goals (non exhaustive):
- Fast optimistic UX offline (local model or cached completions).
- Deterministic conflict resolution where possible (operational transforms for message stream?).
- Incremental, cryptographically verifiable session deltas for audit/privacy.
- Pluggable policies: full-sync, metadata-only, embeddings-only, ephemeral-only.

High-level approach: "deltas + compact index"
- Represent a session as a linear ordered stream of events (user message, assistant output, edit, system instruction). Each event has: event_id (uuid), seq_no (monotonic per-device), client_id, timestamp, op_type, payload (short), signatures(optional).
- Local device maintains current view and a small append-only delta log of events since last sync with server (or with peer).
- Server keeps canonical stream + tombstones for deletions and a compact index (hash chain checkpoints).
- Sync protocol exchanges checkpoints -> server responds with missing ranges or rejects with merge token.

ASCII flow: (client A offline, client B online)
1) clientA: writes events e101..e105 to local log (seq 101-105).
2) clientB (online): writes e201..e205 to server stream.
3) clientA comes online:
   - sends checkpoint: last_seen_server_seq=200, last_local_seq=105, last_hash=H200
   - server computes overlapping range and returns server_events(201..205) + merge_hint
   - clientA applies server_events locally; we try causal ordering: events are ordered by wall-time tiebreaker + client_id priority
   - conflicts: e.g., both clients edited same message -> produce edit-op with intent metadata and keep both versions in tombstone until user resolves

Conflict resolution rules (first pass):
- Add-only operations: simple append, preserve order by (server_seq if present else local_seq + client_id).
- Edits: create new edit event; original message marked edited with parent_event_id. If two edits target same parent, keep both and mark as conflict. Present to user or run auto-merge (semantic merge of assistant responses?).
- Deletes: tombstone pattern; deletions carry reason tag (user, retention, compliance). Tombstones themselves are append-only so they replicate.

Security / privacy sketch:
- Default: transport TLS to server.
- For private deployments / sensitive sessions, allow client-side envelope encryption for payloads before sync. Server stores only metadata and encrypted blobs. Key management: integrate with KMS or client-generated ephemeral keys.
- Signed checkpoints: devices sign checkpoints with device key to prevent rollback attacks. Server keeps attestation of last checkpoint per-device.

Compact checkpoint format (text sketch):
- { device_id, last_seen_server_seq, last_local_seq, checkpoint_hash, sig(device_key) }
- checkpoint_hash = H(H(server_seq_checkpoint) || H(local_delta_range))

API extension proposals (minimal changes):
- POST /sessions/:id/sync-checkpoint  -> body: checkpoint 
  - response: { server_events: [event], server_seq: N, merge_hint: optional }
- POST /sessions/:id/upload-blobs -> body: [encrypted blobs], returns blob_ids
- GET /sessions/:id/delta?after=seq -> streaming response of events (good for resumable sync)

Offline execution model options (tradeoffs):
1) Local small LLM + cached prefix KV: best latency offline, heavier client install.
2) Local policy + staged remote: local policy runs filters and only allow sync of embeddings or indexes.
3) Cached completions only: only last N assistant outputs cached; offline replies from cache with freshness warning.

Edge cases and TODOs (lots):
- How to handle server-side model rollouts that are not backward compatible (tokenization changes?) If client has local model with different tokenizer, merging assistant outputs may be inconsistent. Need version-tagging for models and a fallback flow.
- Large binary payloads (multimodal): prefer blob upload separate from event stream, sync via blob ids.
- Rate limiting & billing: ensure offline local usage isn't billed; only server-side model calls billed. Need to surface to user & telemetry.
- Retention & GDPR: if user requests deletion, ensure tombstones replicate to clients on next sync and encrypted blobs deleted or access revoked. Key rotation scenario: re-encrypt or drop access to past blobs.
- Conflict UX: best-effort auto-merge vs manual, include heuristics (small diffs auto-merge, large changes prompt resolution).

Sample event schema (sketch):
- event_id: uuid-v4
- seq_no: integer (local monotonic)
- client_id: string
- timestamp: ISO8601
- type: [user_msg | assistant_msg | edit | delete | system]
- parent_event_id: optional
- payload_ref: inline small text || blob_id
- meta: { model_version, safety_tags, is_offline_generated }
- sig: optional base64(device_sig)

Example delta snippet (text):
[{
  event_id: "e4c2-...",
  seq_no: 104,
  client_id: "samira-phone",
  timestamp: "2025-06-14T18:12:03Z",
  type: "user_msg",
  payload_ref: "Hey, summarize my notes from this week",
  meta: "{model_hint: "gpt-small-local"}"
}]

Operational notes / storage sizing rough calc:
- Typical session delta per conversation turn: 1–3 KB (small text).
- For 10k active offline devices syncing once/day -> 30MB/day aggregated deltas (server).
- Keep checkpoints + 7 days of deltas for reconciliation; archival beyond that.

Open implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0: PoC local client library that records events and can produce checkpoint hash + handshake with server (no encryption).
- Phase 1: Add server endpoints, blob storage, and linearizable checkpoint verification. Begin UX surface for conflict resolution in console.
- Phase 2: Add client-side encryption, per-tenant policies, and retention controls.
- Phase 3: Optimize incremental embeddings-only sync (for semantic search across devices).

Immediate TODOs for me:
- Draft minimal request/response JSON examples for POST /sync-checkpoint (to add to GH issue).
- Talk with SRE about storing 7-day deltas vs full stream retention cost.
- Quick prototype: mobile app that can append events offline and reconcile with dev server.

Notes to self: keep this protocol composable with existing Redwood routing/fallbacks. Do NOT assume every customer will enable client-side encryption — make it opt-in for enterprise/private deployments.

Questions to collaborators:
- Ethan: how much complexity are we willing to accept in server-side merge logic? Do we want to offload merge to clients?
- Marceline: any compliance blockers for keeping encrypted blobs without plaintext on server?

Misc brainstorm fragments (unresolved):
- Could we store a minimal ‘‘semantic fingerprint’’ per event (embedding) so server can do de-dup detection without plaintext? Might help with dedup and storage.
- Use CRDT? Pros: commutative merges. Cons: chat semantics are ordered and edits complicate pure CRDT approach.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate into a concise PRD if this direction gets thumbs-up.

-- Samira
